parsed.attack: Margin is genuinely safe - thirty photographed bills a month is under 100k input tokens, a few cents at $0.10/M, well inside the $0.30 ceiling - so the attack is acquisition and the residual human. Kill line 2 demands 95% line-level agreement across 1,000 documents, which on a five-year Medicaid lookback still leaves dozens of wrong lines with a five-figure penalty period attached; families will not accept 'confirm the flagged ones' as the only QA, and the instant a person verifies categorisations the wage floor that killed Fin and Clara Labs returns - one hour a month at a $25 loaded rate against a $24.99 subscription netting $21. Worse, the named loop only recruits the second sibling: the first sibling has no channel at all, and the intent keywords that reach them (Medicaid lookback, elder law) run $15-50 CPC, which at a 10% click-to-install and 20% install-to-pay is $750-2,500 per paying user, 30-100x the blended $5.84 CPI.
parsed.strongest_defence: Elder-law attorneys and geriatric care managers refer this at zero cost because it makes their own filings cleaner, $24.99-39/month is trivial against a penalty period worth tens of thousands, and the five-year documentation window gives a multi-year LTV that repays even an $80 cost per paying user inside four months - the highest-margin, longest-lifetime shape in this whole set.
parsed.verdict_reason: Price and margin are genuinely strong, but there is no named channel for the first paying household and the only targetable intent keywords cost 30-100x a blended install.
